nodes.title: director31: 28 lessons on release 52's code (4 pilots, 3 staged), 7 Opus judges by hand: 3 topics pass every gate line (c5-t01, c6, staged c5-t03); c4 fails on a stated wrong rule, c5-t02 on promises 3, the staged c4-ch01-t02 and c6-ch07-t01 fail

After director31: the first staged lesson goes live; a Hindi form is plainer or not written; a rule is true or not said; a picture always draws something new; the short ask by kind of help; an independent cold read of every script before a paid run

Main's script and dry reads check lines against boards and miss two classes: a stated rule that is false as mathematics, and a joint said in the wrong place; both were in front of main before director31 and were found by judges
A behaviour described to judges as by design before a run (the caption read back over a board with no second view) still counts against the gate line it breaks
A Hindi form written as the card's question with words reordered, after a line promising easier words: heard as the same sentence in six topics, promises 3 in one
Answering a picture request over a board with no second view by saying the board's own caption: nothing new is drawn; two judges find it does not help

md.measurements: - `ms-r8-director31` (2026-11-18): 28 lessons (the four pilots and the first three staged scripts `c5-maths-ch02-t03`, `c4-maths-ch01-t02`, `c6-maths-ch07-t01` × steady, stuck, offtopic, steering), Director only, reactive rule-based child, on int/r6 integration 86 (`dba4423b6`, release 52's code), one invocation, 2,294 model calls, about $1.69. Live predicate check exit 0, every gated predicate 0; 28 of 28 picture turns draw the board named (main by hand, then each judge). Seven Opus judges at high effort, one per topic, each reading four lessons by hand against a prompt whose 27 clauses were fixed before the run. By hand, all seven topics: 0 misgrades, 0 unsaid boards (strict reading), every keyed answer given a verdict (686 of 686), beats 98 to 100%. Gate: **pass** c5-t01 (axes 3.5, 4, 4, 4.5, 3.5, 3.5), c6 (3.5, 4, 4, 4.5, 3.5, 4), c5-t03 staged (3.5, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 3.5, 4). **Fail** c4 (axes all at or above 3.5; a stated wrong rule on 3 rows, counted as a false key by main's ruling against the judge's lenient reading; the sentence was in director30 too), c5-t02 (promises 3: four Hindi requests answered with near-copies of the card), c4-ch01-t02 staged (worked example 3, class level 3, promises 3; six false back-to joints from a code path matching a card by its last sentence; four picture turns with nothing new drawn), c6-ch07-t01 staged (two picture turns with nothing new drawn over word tables; a stated wrong rule on 2 rows; axes all at or above 3.5). Steady check-in turns 7, 5, 6, 4 | 4, 5, 7 (director30 pilots 4, 5, 4, 4); 6 turns over 75 words (76 to 80), all the first teaching turn after the start line. Method limits: scripted children, not real ones; one judge per topic, so an axis at the floor rests on one reader; main overruled a judge's count in two topics and says so in the judgement. Judgement: `docs/design/round7/judgements/director31-2026-11-18.md`; results `evals/hybrid-side-by-side/results/2026-11-18-director31/`.
md.decisions: - `dc-r8-director31` (2026-11-18, main, supersedes `dc-r8-director30`): eleven items in `docs/design/round7/judgements/director31-2026-11-18.md`. In short: (1) a `hindi` form is a different, plainer sentence, the switch line promises only Hindi, and a card with no honest plainer form has none; (2) at an asked step a yes gets the question once more and then the easier wording, and steps and the closing question get an authored re-ask; (3) the short ask only straight after the card's own hint, and "back to the earlier question" by the card's identity; (4) the verdict, point and card turn fits 65 words in the script, or the pair is listed whole; (5) a picture request always draws something new (second views from Studio, or an authored second drawing), and a reason is never read as a request; (6) help answers the mistake (the card's second reason before the point's other wording; a give-up at a bridge goes on); (7) every script is read cold by an independent reader before a paid run; (8) the two failed staged scripts are rewritten and heard again; (9) small record and wording items; (10) `c5-maths-ch02-t03` goes live as judged; (11) the next three staged scripts are written under a brief carrying items 1 to 8 and join a run only after the independent read and main's. Clause 2's written remedy (the point and its card a turn of their own after every verdict) is not applied, and the judgement says why: it would put a check-in after every right answer, which `dc-r8-director28` removed on evidence. **Reverses if:** see "What would reverse this" in the judgement (per item: c5-t03 failing next run for a script cause returns it to staged; two judges finding the new Hindi forms harder drops the forms; a pilot failing for a code cause stops the staged batches until two runs in a row pass).
md.rejected:
- `rj-r8-hindi-form-as-reordered-card` (2026-11-18): **tried** giving every card a `hindi` form (Learning 019) checked only for being the same question with no English a home word replaces; the walk says an easier-words line and then the form. **What broke:** in six of seven topics the form is the card with a word changed or the clauses reordered ("Ek poora chakkar kitne metre ka hua?" → "Poora ek chakkar lagaya, toh kitne metre hue?"); five judges heard a promise of easier words followed by the same sentence, and one scored promises 3, failing c5-t02. In the class 4 angles lesson the form swapped "right angle" for "samkon", which is harder. Replaced by `dc-r8-director31` item 1 and a checker rule on word overlap.
- `rj-r8-caption-as-picture-over-viewless-board` (2026-11-18): **tried** answering a picture request over a board that has no second view (angle, shape, measured, word table) by saying that board's authored caption, and told the judges it was by design. **What broke:** the gate already lists a picture request answered with nothing new drawn as a contradiction; two judges found it does not help ("drawing karke samjhao" answered by a word table read back) and six rows count against two staged scripts. Replaced by `dc-r8-director31` item 5: second views, or an authored second drawing, and the checker fails a card with neither.
